evidence.title: Install
evidence.finding: macOS only (not available for Windows or Linux yet); setup checks GitHub auth and at least one of Claude, Codex or Cursor credentials.

evidence.title: Conductor
evidence.locator: Hero; Multiplayer; Cloud sandboxes; agent list; Conduct from anywhere; latest release link
evidence.finding: Vendor homepage presents a team of coding agents running in the cloud, isolated cloud workspaces, and shared workspaces where teammates can follow work and prompt together in real time. It names Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode. The Conduct from anywhere section links macOS, the iOS App Store and the API; the latest release link is 0.90.0 (Conductor for iOS, 2026-10-02).

evidence.title: Pricing
evidence.locator: Free, Pro, Teams, Enterprise; cloud fee FAQ; SOC 2 FAQ
evidence.finding: Plans: Free $0 (local workspaces on a Mac, own subscriptions and keys); Pro $50/mo with no per-user or per-account qualifier (Conductor Cloud and "a bunch of cloud workspace hours", multiplayer with up to 5 Pro users, Conductor API, "Conductor mobile app"); Teams $60/mo/user, invite-only (admin portal, centralized billing); Enterprise custom (DPA, SAML SSO, SCIM, SLA). No trial or card text. FAQ: no extra Cloud fee now, usage-based compute pricing planned. SOC 2 Type II statement. Page undated.

evidence.title: Cloud FAQ
evidence.locator: Features and plans; Cloud specifications; Security
evidence.finding: Cloud on Pro, Teams and Enterprise; Teams invite-only with an admin portal "to manage user roles"; Teams members can collaborate "by sharing workspaces and prompting agents together in real time"; no extra fee now, usage-based compute pricing planned; sandboxes have 8 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM and 32 GB ephemeral NVMe; Vercel sandboxes in us-east-1; GitHub only; own cloud machines "Not yet", self-hosted offering being built. The Pro answer still says "our mobile app (coming soon)". Page undated.

evidence.title: Conductor Cloud
evidence.locator: Cloud Computer; Local and Cloud workspaces
evidence.finding: Each agent runs in its own isolated cloud sandbox and keeps working after the laptop closes until the sandbox sleeps; "The chat, diff, git, terminal, and pull request workflow is the same in both" local and cloud. Support via Help > Send Feedback or humans@conductor.build. Page undated. Local vs Cloud table: "After your Mac closes | Local processes stop | Agents keep running until the sandbox sleeps".

evidence.title: Multiplayer
evidence.locator: Shared chat; Home; Hand off a workspace
evidence.finding: Cloud organization workspaces are shared with the team; transcripts update live; presence dots for active teammates and typing indicators in a shared chat; Home filters by teammate and project; follow and reassign workspaces; direct links. The page does not describe co-prompting, private workspaces, roles or plan limits. Page undated.

evidence.title: Workflow
evidence.locator: Workspace per shippable unit; Run agents independently
evidence.finding: Workspace is the delegation unit; branch/PR is integration unit. GitHub/Linear intake and repository instructions are documented.

evidence.title: First workspace
evidence.locator: Repository; Make it runnable; Start work
evidence.finding: Repository options: "Open project" (existing local repository), "Open GitHub project" and "Quick start" (new repository). Setup and run scripts; chats with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode; gh auth status check. No text on repositories without a remote or non-git folders. Page undated.

evidence.title: Parallel agents
evidence.finding: Independent branches or multiple agents sharing one checkout; shared-file collision risk is explicit.

evidence.title: Cloud workspaces
evidence.locator: Sleep and maximum lifetime; Forward ports; Sync
evidence.finding: Four-hour inactivity sleep; 23h50m hard lifetime. Files/chat persist, processes stop and interrupted turns need resending.

evidence.title: Diff viewer
evidence.finding: Unified/commit-filtered diffs, line feedback and GitHub review comments. "Conductor recommends actions as a workspace moves toward merge. Use those actions to create a pull request, respond to feedback, fix checks, and merge". Page undated.

evidence.title: Checks
evidence.finding: Checks may include Git status, "Pull request metadata", CI and status checks, "Deployments", GitHub comments and review threads, and todos. Blockers: "Conductor may block or discourage merge actions when required work is still open, such as unresolved todos or failed checks", so enforcement strength is not established. Page undated.

evidence.title: Todos
evidence.locator: How todos work; Send todos to agent
evidence.finding: Humans and agents use workspace todos; unchecked todos block merge; @todos exposes list to agent.

evidence.title: Checkpoints
evidence.finding: Checkpoints are stored locally as private Git refs, captured "Before each supported agent responds" (agents not named); restoring a turn deletes that turn and later messages and reverts code changes since. Page undated.

evidence.title: Conductor API
evidence.locator: Introduction; Quick start (for AI); Authentication; Endpoints; Routines; Cookbook; Tips
evidence.finding: Beta HTTP API under https://api.conductor.build/v0 with an OpenAPI document; bearer API key; endpoints for projects, workspaces (create, get, rename, archive, unarchive, sleep), sessions, prompts, transcripts, cancel ("drop queued messages"), SQL and routines. Routines created through the API run a saved prompt in a fresh workspace on each webhook JSON POST. Cookbook: "messages sent while it works are steered into the running turn"; Tips: a queued prompt reports idle until its turn starts. Some 403s come from a proxy that rejects default client signatures (send a User-Agent). Shows a routine example with the `conductor` CLI. No SDK is documented on this page. Quick start (for AI) requires a Conductor Pro account to generate an API key. Page undated. Endpoint table: GET /v0/sessions/{id}/status "Whether the agent is idle, working, or errored"; POST /v0/sessions/{id}/cancel "Stop the agent's current turn and drop queued messages". Tips: "Always pass an explicit model" (workspace creation, POST /v0/workspaces) and "An optional effort field sets the thinking level for claude and codex sessions". No sidebar-section endpoint listed.

evidence.title: Conductor MCP server
evidence.finding: Beta hosted MCP ("Tools and input shapes may change"): OAuth limited to mcp:tools and one organization, or bearer API key. Tools include create_session, send_message ("Send or queue a prompt for a session"), cancel_session ("Cancel the current agent turn and discard queued messages"), get_session_status ("Get a session's current agent status", no values listed), list_models, list_messages (after cursor), get_message and run_sql. No routine or section tools listed. Page undated.

evidence.title: Security and permissions
evidence.finding: Cloud agents run in isolated Linux sandboxes hosted by Vercel and can use the workspace environment variables and secrets; repository files and session data are kept in Conductor-managed infrastructure. Local agents run with the user account permissions; approvals can be required for shell commands, file changes, MCP tool calls or web fetches. Page undated.

evidence.title: Conductor 0.85.0
evidence.finding: Routines run agents on a schedule or via GitHub action, in the cloud, so Pro and Team only (no webhook text on this page); private workspaces; favorite models sync across devices in cloud organizations; Cursor subscription sign-in for cloud workspaces; per-organization cloud agent connections; "Plans, screenshots, and attachments in .context now sync from cloud workspaces to your Mac"; experimental workspace status matrix. Model picker shortcuts change models, effort and speed.

evidence.locator: Release notes; Improvements; Fixes; Misc; New in 0.90.1

evidence.title: Agent modes

evidence.title: Isolated workspaces
evidence.finding: Each workspace is a git worktree on its own branch; a branch can be checked out in one workspace at a time; states workspace isolation is development isolation, not a security boundary, and agents run on the Mac with user permissions.

evidence.title: Harnesses
evidence.finding: Four harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are bundled; Cursor sessions use Cursor Agent through the Cursor API. One harness and model per chat tab. "Conductor is free to use. We do not bill or resell model usage." Page undated.

evidence.title: Configure model providers
evidence.locator: Harness auth; Claude Code compatible providers
evidence.finding: Claude Code via CLI auth or API key mode (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or compatible providers (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Bedrock, GLM); Codex via "Codex sign-in, an OpenAI subscription, or an API key" (CODEX_API_KEY) or gateway; OpenCode via provider credentials; Cursor via Cursor API key. "Conductor does not bill or resell model usage." Local models and Vertex AI not covered. Page undated.

evidence.title: Managed settings
evidence.finding: Provisional organization-controlled settings file on a Mac overrides user and repository settings (for example enterprise_data_privacy, default models, environment variables).

evidence.title: Cloud Computer
evidence.locator: Specifications; Builds; Setup scripts; Environment variables and secrets
evidence.finding: Each cloud workspace runs in an isolated microVM with 8 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and 32 GB ephemeral NVMe. The Cloud Computer is the shared development environment for a Conductor organization; the page gives no Cloud Computer disk size; up to 50 GitHub repositories; successful builds seed new workspaces; saved secrets are hidden but exposed as env vars inside workspaces; an Admin workspace agent can edit install/setup scripts and run builds.

evidence.title: Set up cloud
evidence.locator: Requirements; Setup steps; Admin and credentials
evidence.finding: Cloud onboarding: create organization, connect the Conductor GitHub App, add an agent credential (subscription token or API key), build the Cloud Computer, then work in an Admin workspace. Admins can add shared API keys that take precedence over personal keys.

evidence.title: From issue to pull request
evidence.locator: Starting a workspace from an issue; Creating the pull request
evidence.finding: A workspace can be started from a GitHub or Linear issue and inherits its title, description and context; Create PR sends the diff and repository context to the agent to draft the PR. Issue-PR linking is not described. After the PR exists, use Checks and Diff Viewer "to respond to CI, deployments, review comments, and todos".

evidence.title: Review and merge a workspace
evidence.locator: Review flow; Checks; Merge and archive
evidence.finding: Diff viewer, Review action (agent reviews diff), Checks tab; unresolved comments, failing checks and open todos are to be treated as blockers; merge, then archive.

evidence.title: Privacy
evidence.locator: Data storage; Telemetry; Enterprise data privacy
evidence.finding: Cloud session inputs and outputs are stored on Conductor servers; local session data stays on the Mac (~/Library/Application Support/com.conductor.app); analytics and crash logs via PostHog, including OS and IP address. No export, deletion or retention text. Enterprise data privacy is local-only and "cannot be used in cloud". Page undated.

evidence.title: Settings reference
evidence.finding: Settings include tool_approvals_enabled, Codex tool_approval_policy (default or always_approve), default plan mode, review/PR/conflict prompts, git.archive_on_merge, enterprise_data_privacy.

evidence.title: Environment variables

evidence.title: FAQ

evidence.title: Conductor Cloud
evidence.locator: Cloud Computer; Local and Cloud workspaces
evidence.finding: Each agent runs in its own isolated cloud sandbox and keeps working after the laptop closes until the sandbox sleeps; "The chat, diff, git, terminal, and pull request workflow is the same in both" local and cloud. Support via Help > Send Feedback or humans@conductor.build. Page undated. Local vs Cloud table: "After your Mac closes | Local processes stop | Agents keep running until the sandbox sleeps".

evidence.title: Cloud workspaces
evidence.locator: Sleep and maximum lifetime; Forward ports; Sync
evidence.finding: Cloud inactivity sleep is now 20 minutes without agent or terminal activity; focused window counts as activity. Maximum lifetime remains 23h50m even when active. Files and chats survive sleep; processes stop and interrupted turns must be resent.

evidence.title: Conductor API
evidence.locator: Introduction; Quick start (for AI); Authentication; Endpoints; Routines; Cookbook; Tips
evidence.finding: Beta HTTP API under https://api.conductor.build/v0 with an OpenAPI document; bearer API key; endpoints for projects, workspaces (create, get, rename, archive, unarchive, sleep), sessions, prompts, transcripts, cancel ("drop queued messages"), SQL and routines. Routines created through the API run a saved prompt in a fresh workspace on each webhook JSON POST. Cookbook: "messages sent while it works are steered into the running turn"; Tips: a queued prompt reports idle until its turn starts. Some 403s come from a proxy that rejects default client signatures (send a User-Agent). Shows a routine example with the `conductor` CLI. No SDK is documented on this page. Quick start (for AI) requires a Conductor Pro account to generate an API key. Page undated. Endpoint table: GET /v0/sessions/{id}/status "Whether the agent is idle, working, or errored"; POST /v0/sessions/{id}/cancel "Stop the agent's current turn and drop queued messages". Tips: "Always pass an explicit model" (workspace creation, POST /v0/workspaces) and "An optional effort field sets the thinking level for claude and codex sessions". No sidebar-section endpoint listed.

evidence.title: Conductor MCP server
evidence.finding: Beta hosted MCP ("Tools and input shapes may change"): OAuth limited to mcp:tools and one organization, or bearer API key. Tools include create_session, send_message ("Send or queue a prompt for a session"), cancel_session ("Cancel the current agent turn and discard queued messages"), get_session_status ("Get a session's current agent status", no values listed), list_models, list_messages (after cursor), get_message and run_sql. No routine or section tools listed. Page undated.

evidence.title: Conductor Remote Control
evidence.finding: Experimental feature: the Conductor iOS app pairs with a Mac by QR code and can browse and create local workspaces, read chats, send messages, pick models, stop agents and archive workspaces. evidence.title: Conductor harness reference
evidence.finding: The complete harness comparison lists Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are bundled; Cursor uses the Cursor API. Conductor is explicitly free to use and does not bill or resell model usage; provider accounts or keys pay inference.

evidence.title: Conductor current clients
evidence.locator: Conduct from anywhere; Bring your own subscriptions; Multiplayer
evidence.finding: The client selector offers macOS, iOS and API access. The page names the fixed four harnesses and explicitly describes teammates prompting agents together in real time. It does not offer Android or a browser ADE client in this complete client selector.

evidence.title: Conductor updated announcement
evidence.finding: The earlier shutdown paragraph is struck through. The updated announcement says development will continue and the FAQ says Conductor keeps working as normal. The previous wind-down deadlines are not a basis for new capability or price mappings.

evidence.title: Conductor terms
evidence.finding: The terms explicitly define the Platform as proprietary hosted AI automation software including client-side and hosted software. They retain vendor intellectual property and grant restricted platform access.

evidence.title: Conductor Cloud runtime FAQ
evidence.locator: Cloud specifications; data privacy; own cloud machines
evidence.finding: Conductor provisions a Vercel sandbox for each Cloud workspace, keeps Cloud sessions on its servers, and does not yet support user-supplied cloud machines. Local sessions stop when the Mac closes. The plan-family section includes an outdated mobile-app coming-soon sentence, so this pass does not use it to reconstruct current commercial entitlements. The Enterprise description names automated user provisioning without specifying its protocol.

evidence.title: Conductor Cloud overview
evidence.locator: Local and Cloud workspaces; Cloud organization
evidence.finding: The current overview explicitly states that agents continue after the laptop closes. Its comparison distinguishes local Mac processes from hosted Linux sandboxes, which continue until the sandbox sleeps. Workspaces and chats are shared within the organization.

evidence.title: Conductor Cloud organization onboarding
evidence.locator: Create or select the organization; Add an agent
evidence.finding: Members joining an already configured organization add their agent credentials as needed. Organization admins can additionally configure shared agent API keys for the organization; those keys override a member personal key for the same agent. Organization creation includes optional teammate invitations.
